## Overview

Move `HummingMoEMethod` expert selection, weight conversion, quant configuration, and kernel construction into `fused_moe/oracle/humming.py`, addressing the Humming portion of #54959. Checkpoint parameter creation/loading stays in the quantization method.

## Claims

- Preserve existing kernel preference and execution behavior while putting MoE setup behind the oracle boundary.
- Incorporate merged #56685: retain its modular schema/linear helpers, runtime input-schema fallback, Hadamard handling, and input-scale propagation. Update the new W4A8 caller as well as existing callers.
- Shared `HummingMoEQuantConfig` and its factory remain in `quantization/utils/humming/moe.py`; no quantization modes or expert kernels are added.
- Preserve the upstream `prefers_humming` and `prioritize_humming` exports introduced by #56997 when resolving the latest merge conflict.

## Validation

Revalidated after resolving conflicts against main `cc9b0f097d49abfa6fc94d1d773dca1cc2b9619c` on October 12, 2026:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Humming CUDA pytest | 33 passed, 1144 deselected |
| Oracle/quantization pytest | 56 passed, 1 skipped |
| 16 CUDA baseline/candidate cases | All bitwise identical |
| GSM8K, 64 questions, 5-shot | 15/64 → 15/64 (23.4375% on both) |
| Generated token sequences | 64/64 identical; 10,223 output tokens on each side |
| Actual model backend | All 24 MoE layers use `HummingMoEMethod` |
| Relevant pre-commit checks, Buildkite test tethering, mypy (Python 3.11) | Passed |

Pytest commands, run from `tests/` with `PYTHONPATH` unset:

```bash
../.venv/bin/python -m pytest kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k humming -q --disable-warnings
../.venv/bin/python -m pytest kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py \
  quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
  quantization/test_moe_wna16.py quantization/test_humming_ignore.py \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

The CUDA comparison covers indexed/grouped experts, BF16/FP16, SiLU/non-gated ReLU², 1/17 tokens, a nonidentity expert map, and repeated post-load processing. Each case also matches its PyTorch reference. AST checks confirm that eight relocated functions and the two retained configuration definitions match current main; schema-key derivation and fallback are equivalent after scope renaming.

<details>
<summary>Model evaluation and environment</summary>

The existing `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py::evaluate_gsm8k_offline` harness was used with temperature 0, max_tokens 256, seed 42, FP16, eager execution, and prefix caching disabled. It read cached official GSM8K records with prompt/generation/scoring logic unchanged.

Model: [`wantsleep/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-4bit-autogptq`](https://huggingface.co/wantsleep/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-4bit-autogptq/tree/6c93a26b639beb8156f66aedcb345c7aed3410e2), revision `6c93a26b639beb8156f66aedcb345c7aed3410e2`. The existing validation checkpoint uses a lossless external adaptation of legacy expert names/layout to standard gate/up/down projections, with exact reconstruction assertions; both revisions used the same adapted checkpoint. No quantized values were changed. These are sampled output-parity results, not a performance claim.

Environment: one RTX 4090, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cu132, humming-kernels 0.1.16, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA toolkit 13.0. Main/MoE native extensions come from the official `3fe917abb13160d60bea5330399f5c09ca282348` wheel; the only commit between that wheel and the validation base changes Python code and does not change C++/CUDA sources. Other dependencies/native artifacts are reused from the existing isolated environment. This is not a full native rebuild or the exact upstream CI image. Multi-GPU EP/all-to-all and Hopper/Blackwell/ROCm/XPU execution were not tested.

Relevant Python pre-commit hooks ran on changed files; unrelated language/build hooks were skipped. The current official `mypy` hook targets Python 3.11 and passed.

</details>

## Details

The scope was recorded in [the issue before implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54959#issuecomment-5726903544). #56306 and #56523 concern other MXFP4 methods; #43373 established the Humming helpers. #56685 has now merged, and this update adapts the migration to its implementation instead of retaining the old utility layout. The tracker includes additional work and is not closed by this PR. The linear-method migration is outside this change.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, conflict resolution, validation, and this description.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Preserves the existing oracle boundary and upstream Humming behavior without new kernels or core execution branches.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Relevant tests and current-main model comparisons passed; hardware and environment limits are recorded above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Relevant pre-commit checks and mypy passed; no new user-facing feature requires documentation.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes scope, related work, reproduction commands, evidence, and limitations.

</details>

## Overview

Move `HummingMoEMethod` expert selection, weight conversion, quant configuration, and kernel construction into `fused_moe/oracle/humming.py`, addressing the Humming portion of #54959. Checkpoint parameter creation/loading stays in the quantization method.

## Claims

- Preserve existing kernel preference and execution behavior while putting MoE setup behind the oracle boundary.
- Incorporate merged #56685: retain its modular schema/linear helpers, runtime input-schema fallback, Hadamard handling, and input-scale propagation. Update the new W4A8 caller as well as existing callers.
- Shared `HummingMoEQuantConfig` and its factory remain in `quantization/utils/humming/moe.py`; no quantization modes or expert kernels are added.
- Preserve the upstream `prefers_humming` and `prioritize_humming` exports introduced by #56997 when resolving the latest merge conflict.

## Validation

Revalidated after resolving conflicts against main `cc9b0f097d49abfa6fc94d1d773dca1cc2b9619c` on October 12, 2026:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Humming CUDA pytest | 33 passed, 1144 deselected |
| Oracle/quantization pytest | 56 passed, 1 skipped |
| 16 CUDA baseline/candidate cases | All bitwise identical |
| GSM8K, 64 questions, 5-shot | 15/64 → 15/64 (23.4375% on both) |
| Generated token sequences | 64/64 identical; 10,223 output tokens on each side |
| Actual model backend | All 24 MoE layers use `HummingMoEMethod` |
| Relevant pre-commit checks, Buildkite test tethering, mypy (Python 3.11) | Passed |

Pytest commands, run from `tests/` with `PYTHONPATH` unset:

```bash
../.venv/bin/python -m pytest kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k humming -q --disable-warnings
../.venv/bin/python -m pytest kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py \
  quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
  quantization/test_moe_wna16.py quantization/test_humming_ignore.py \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

The CUDA comparison covers indexed/grouped experts, BF16/FP16, SiLU/non-gated ReLU², 1/17 tokens, a nonidentity expert map, and repeated post-load processing. Each case also matches its PyTorch reference. AST checks confirm that eight relocated functions and the two retained configuration definitions match current main; schema-key derivation and fallback are equivalent after scope renaming.

<details>
<summary>Model evaluation and environment</summary>

The existing `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py::evaluate_gsm8k_offline` harness was used with temperature 0, max_tokens 256, seed 42, FP16, eager execution, and prefix caching disabled. It read cached official GSM8K records with prompt/generation/scoring logic unchanged.

Model: [`wantsleep/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-4bit-autogptq`](https://huggingface.co/wantsleep/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct-4bit-autogptq/tree/6c93a26b639beb8156f66aedcb345c7aed3410e2), revision `6c93a26b639beb8156f66aedcb345c7aed3410e2`. The existing validation checkpoint uses a lossless external adaptation of legacy expert names/layout to standard gate/up/down projections, with exact reconstruction assertions; both revisions used the same adapted checkpoint. No quantized values were changed. These are sampled output-parity results, not a performance claim.

Environment: one RTX 4090, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cu132, humming-kernels 0.1.16, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA toolkit 13.0. Main/MoE native extensions come from the official `3fe917abb13160d60bea5330399f5c09ca282348` wheel; the only commit between that wheel and the validation base changes Python code and does not change C++/CUDA sources. Other dependencies/native artifacts are reused from the existing isolated environment. This is not a full native rebuild or the exact upstream CI image. Multi-GPU EP/all-to-all and Hopper/Blackwell/ROCm/XPU execution were not tested.

Relevant Python pre-commit hooks ran on changed files; unrelated language/build hooks were skipped. The current official `mypy` hook targets Python 3.11 and passed.

</details>

The scope was recorded in [the issue before implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54959#issuecomment-5726903544). #56306 and #56523 concern other MXFP4 methods; #43373 established the Humming helpers. #56685 has now merged, and this update adapts the migration to its implementation instead of retaining the old utility layout. The tracker includes additional work and is not closed by this PR. The linear-method migration is outside this change.

+def _replace_layer_parameters(
+    layer: "RoutedExperts",
+    sublayer_name: str,
+    tensors: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+    preserve_bias: bool = False,

+    """Replace layer parameters for a sublayer with new tensors.
+
+    Args:
+        layer: The RoutedExperts layer

+        tensors: Dict of parameter name to tensor
+        preserve_bias: If True, don't delete bias parameters

+    # Delete old parameters
+    for name, _ in list(layer.named_parameters()):

+        tensors=tensors,

-def _process_single_sublayer(

-    """Process a single sublayer: convert, optionally requant, prepare, and transform.

-    This combines the common logic from convert_to_humming_moe_kernel_format
-    for processing a single sublayer.
-
-    Args:
-        layer: The RoutedExperts layer
-        sublayer_name: Name of the sublayer (e.g., "w13", "w2")
-        shape_n: Output dimension size
-        shape_k: Input dimension size
-        weight_schema: Initial weight quantization schema
-        input_schema: Initial input quantization schema
-        has_bias: Whether the layer has bias terms
-        num_experts: Number of experts
-        param_dtype: Parameter data type
-        force_weight_schema: Optional schema to force requantization to
-        allow_input_schema_fallback: Whether incompatible input schemas may be replaced.

-    Returns:

-    """
-    from vllm.utils.humming import HummingWeightSchema
-
-    # Step 1: Convert from checkpoint format to humming format if needed
-    current_weight_schema, current_input_schema = _convert_sublayer_to_humming(
-        layer=layer,

-        source_tensors = _extract_sublayer_tensors(layer, sublayer_name)

-        if name is not None:

-
-        current_weight_schema = force_weight_schema
-        _replace_layer_parameters(layer, sublayer_name, tensors, preserve_bias=True)
-        del tensors
-
-    # Step 3: Prepare layer metadata and transform weights
-    current_input_schema = humming_schema.check_and_fallback_input_schema(
-        weight_schema=current_weight_schema,
-        input_schema=current_input_schema,
-        param_dtype=param_dtype,
-        allow_fallback=allow_input_schema_fallback,

-        layer=layer,
-        sublayer_name=sublayer_name,
-        shape_n=shape_n,

-    """Convert MoE weights from checkpoint format to Humming kernel format.
-
-    This function processes weights for each sublayer (w13, w2) by:
-    1. Converting from checkpoint format to humming format if needed
-    2. Force requanting if a different quantization schema is specified
-    3. Preparing layer metadata for the Humming kernel
-    4. Transforming weights for inference
-
-    Args:
-        layer: The RoutedExperts layer containing weights to process
-        quant_config: Optional quantization config dict. Required if weight_schema
-                     or input_schema are None. Used to build schemas via
-                     BaseWeightSchema.from_config().
-        sublayer_configs: Optional configuration dict for each sublayer (w13, w2).
-                         Each config must have "shape_n" and "shape_k" keys.
-                         If None, configs are built from layer.moe_config properties.
-        weight_schema: Optional initial weight quantization schema.
-                      If None, built from quant_config.
-        input_schema: Optional initial input quantization schema.
-                     If None, built from quant_config or env vars.
-        force_weight_schema: Optional schema to force requantization to
-        allow_input_schema_fallback: Whether incompatible input schemas may be replaced.
-
-    Side effects:
-        - Modifies layer parameters in place
-        - Sets layer.weight_schemas and layer.input_schemas
-        - Sets layer.humming_configs for quant config construction
-
-    """
-    # Build schemas from quant_config if not provided
-    has_bias = layer.moe_config.has_bias
-    num_experts = layer.moe_config.num_local_experts
-    param_dtype = layer.params_dtype
-
-    if weight_schema is None or input_schema is None:
-        if quant_config is None:
-            raise ValueError(
-                "Must provide either weight_schema/input_schema or quant_config"
-            )
-
-        from vllm.utils.humming import BaseWeightSchema, HummingInputSchema
-
-        if weight_schema is None:
-            weight_schema = BaseWeightSchema.from_config(quant_config)
-
-        if input_schema is None:
-            input_quant_config = (envs.VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG or {}).copy()
-            if humming_is_layer_skipped(input_quant_config, layer.layer_name):
-                input_schema = HummingInputSchema()
-            else:
-                # TODO: read input_quant_config from quant_config
-                input_quant_config = humming_schema.resolve_humming_layer_config(
-                    input_quant_config, layer.layer_name
-                )
-                allow_input_schema_fallback = input_quant_config.pop(
-                    "allow_fallback", False
-                )
-                input_schema = HummingInputSchema.from_config(input_quant_config)
-
-    # Build sublayer configs from layer properties if not provided
-    if sublayer_configs is None:
-        is_gated = layer.moe_config.activation.is_gated
-        intermediate_size = layer.moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition
-        sublayer_configs = {
-            "w13": {
-                "shape_n": intermediate_size * (2 if is_gated else 1),
-                "shape_k": layer.moe_config.hidden_dim,
-            },
-            "w2": {
-                "shape_n": layer.moe_config.hidden_dim,
-                "shape_k": intermediate_size,
-            },
-        }
-
-    layer.weight_schemas = {}
-    layer.input_schemas = {}
-    humming_configs = {}
-
-    for sublayer_name, configs in sublayer_configs.items():
-        final_weight_schema, final_input_schema, humming_config = (
-            _process_single_sublayer(
-                layer=layer,
-                sublayer_name=sublayer_name,
-                shape_n=configs["shape_n"],
-                shape_k=configs["shape_k"],
-                weight_schema=weight_schema,
-                input_schema=input_schema,
-                has_bias=has_bias,
-                num_experts=num_experts,
-                param_dtype=param_dtype,
-                force_weight_schema=force_weight_schema,
-                allow_input_schema_fallback=allow_input_schema_fallback,
-            )
-        )
-
-        layer.weight_schemas[sublayer_name] = final_weight_schema
-        layer.input_schemas[sublayer_name] = final_input_schema
-        humming_configs[sublayer_name] = humming_config
-
-    layer.humming_configs = humming_configs
-    return humming_configs
